pages.text: Create's $(thing)steam engines$() are highly versatile sources of rotational power, but in vanilla, unlocking their efficiency requires the usage of $(l:where_are_blaze_burners)blaze burners$(). Since those are unobtainable in $(#6A2)TerraFirmaCraft$(), their power is instead unlocked via $(thing)fireboxes$()!
Only $(bold)one$() firebox is needed to power a max level steam engine, if you can keep it $(#B53)hot$() enough.
pages.name: A steam engine

pages.title: Using a Firebox
pages.text: When a $(thing)firebox$() is underneath a steam boiler, it has $(bold)3 possible states$():$(br)$(li)$(bold)Cold:$() It is either unlit or it's temperature is under $(bold)$(#888)100ºC$(). In this state, it will provide no heat to the boiler above.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Hot:$() The firebox temperature is between $(bold)$(#888)100ºC$() and $(bold)$(d)2000ºC$(), providing a proportional heat level to the boiler above.

The greater the temperature, the higher the heat level of the boiler.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Super hot:$() The firebox temperature goes above $(bold)$(d)2000ºC$(), this state means it is outputting the $(o)highest heat level possible$() for a steam boiler, and thus one of these can $(bold)fully$() power a max level steam engine by itself.

pages.title: Geothermal power
pages.text: $(thing)Steam engines$() can now also be powered simply by pumping pressurized hot water into them -- $(bold)No external heating needed!$()$(br) Of course, feeding $(thing)spring water$() to a steam boiler also comes at a cost: Boilers require $(t:Configurable in settings)4^$() times as much $(thing)spring water$() as they would regular water!. In exchange, the spring water will actively provide an $(bold)extra$() $(t:Configurable in settings)4^$() heat levels to the boiler.
